items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well then I've got here, (Art Hodes in Chicago 1950... [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yes.

ctx.x: He writes and he arranges a lot too. I see his name sometimes.
Well then I've got here, (Art Hodes in Chicago 1950, Bobby Hackett '51. And that's before joining Bernie Billings in Los Angeles, is that right?

items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: What it did to me was, I got zutty. Now, last time I worked with zutty was on Decca Records. And zutty and I were very together.

ctx.x: That's what eventually killed the Blue Note, according to Frank Holstein. If you wanted Duke, you had to take Joe Blow.

What it did to me was, I got zutty. Now, last time I worked with zutty was on Decca Records. And zutty and I were very together. But now, here I'm not drinking, I'm not smoking, I'm not -- very straight kick. And probably not playing as good, because it takes a while to start -- if you've been playing high and drunk all the time, you get sober, not drink and not get high, it's going to take you a while to find your way around. And that I have to admit, I can't fault nobody.

The other end of the stick is, zutty is way out. I'm not talking about him smoking pot. I mean, he's out there, he's doing something. If it's that much off, a hairline off, it bothers him. Just -- or the tempo or the way I'm playing. And we were not together, right from the start.
